notes:
Account: Northbridge AI (northbridge.ai)

Stage: Evaluation (target close Mar 2026)
Owner: Owen Phillips | SE: Ibrahim Khan

What they’re building
- B2B SaaS "support copilot" that answers agents + drafts customer replies.
- Pipeline: embeddings + retrieval + chat completion (streaming in UI). Some tool-calling in roadmap (ticket lookups, CRM writebacks).
- Spiky usage (customer launches + incident surges). They’ve been burned by "timeouts that look like server issues" from prior provider.

What they care about (verbatim-ish)
- "If you’re overloaded, tell us. Don’t just hang until our gateway times out."
- Wants documented separation of:
  - 429 rate limit / quota / concurrency policy (client should backoff)
  - 503 overload / capacity protection (client should honor Retry-After; they want clear guidance on whether to retry vs fail fast)
- Wants stable, customer-visible error code taxonomy: so they can bucket in their telemetry and write deterministic retries.
- Wants correlation IDs in every failure response; they want to paste into tickets.

Region failover requirements
- Primary region us-east; fallback to us-west when capacity constrained.
- They asked if we do automatic regional failover or if they must set policy. They prefer policy-driven behavior with explicit constraints (no infinite loops, bounded retries, prefer same model family).
- They want to understand what happens during partial brownouts (dependency degradation vs GPU saturation) and how errors differ.

Latency / reliability / cost
- p95 first-token < ~900ms for common prompts; p99 under bursts should degrade via early shedding rather than tail blowups.
- Wants predictable behavior for streaming: if we shed, do so early (before sending partial response), otherwise their UI has messy UX.
- Cost: moderately sensitive; willing to pay for Dedicated if Hosted cannot guarantee stable behavior during bursts.

Security/compliance
- SOC2: required for vendor approval.
- SSO/SAML: required for console access if they expand to multiple teams.
- Audit logs: required (admin events + key management changes).
- Retention controls: asked specifically about request/response logging and how long we keep it.
- Data residency: not required today but flagged for EU expansion H2.

Open questions / next steps
- Provide canonical docs link (or excerpt) describing:
  - HTTP status mapping (429 vs 503)
  - error code fields
  - Retry-After semantics (presence/format/consistency)
  - recommended client retry policy (backoff + jitter, when NOT to retry)
- Confirm routing/failover behavior details: when breaker open, what happens (same region different model vs different region same model), and how customers configure it.
- Schedule technical review w/ routing + SRE if needed; they want to see monitoring/dashboards for shed rate and breaker opens.

Internal notes
- This prospect maps directly to current reliability initiative (hosted circuit breakers + load shedding). They’re effectively asking for the outcomes: early, explicit overload rejection + stable semantics + documented retries + region fallback.
- Risk: if we can’t commit to consistent Retry-After + clear taxonomy across all routes, they’ll default to a bigger provider.
- Upside: strong fit; their team is disciplined about reliability and will be a reference if experience is clean.
